title: Dark Matter promotes three executives to senior leadership roles
excerpt: Dark Matter promoted Don Oliver to CTO, Chris Medvidofsky to CFO, and Blaine Prober to general counsel as it expands AI and APIs.
content:
Article Summary

Dark Matter Technologies promoted 3 executives to senior roles, naming Don Oliver CTO, Chris Medvidofsky CFO, and Blaine Prober general counsel. The moves align with the company’s push to expand APIs, MCP and agentic AI across Empower and Aiva Intelligence.  AI Summary

Dark Matter Technologies announced on Friday that it has promoted three executives to senior leadership roles, naming Don Oliver chief technology officer, Chris Medvidofsky chief financial officer and Blaine Prober general counsel.

All three executives have been with the home lending technology provider since its launch in 2023.

The promotions follow the recent appointments of Salvatore Piccola as senior vice president of product strategy and Gil Valera as vice president of professional services.

As chief technology officer, Oliver will lead the company’s technology organization, including the expansion of application programming interfaces (APIs), Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agentic artificial intelligence capabilities across its Empower loan origination system and Aiva Intelligence platform.

Oliver most recently served as vice president of platform engineering. He also brings experience in Amazon Web Services (AWS) and artificial intelligence and has represented Dark Matter on AI initiatives within Constellation Software.

Medvidofsky, previously vice president of finance and accounting, will oversee the company’s financial strategy and operations. He has managed Dark Matter’s finances since its founding.

Prober will lead the company’s legal and compliance functions as general counsel. He previously served as vice president and deputy general counsel and was lead deal counsel for the Empower platform.

“We invest in people, give them room to grow and move them into larger roles when both they and the company are ready,” Dark Matter CEO Vikas Rao said in a statement. “Don, Chris and Blaine earned these roles through the quality of their work and their commitment to our clients.”

The appointments come as Dark Matter continues to develop its technology platform for mortgage lenders and servicers, with an emphasis on artificial intelligence and automation.

The company’s offerings include the Empower loan origination system, which includes a built-in point-of-sale solution and Aiva Intelligence, as well as the Elevate loan servicing platform and the Exchange partner marketplace.
